second_order: calling people to build Dark Souls pictures
theme_note: Calls, coordinates, recruitment, and first pixels all enlist others in beginning recognizable Dark Souls images; what varies is the proposed image and location.

second_order: learning how the canvas and painted flair work
theme_note: Questions and answers make the event usable by explaining placement intervals, palette constraints, and the painted flair.

second_order: funneling helpers into a workable shared plan
theme_note: Participants redirect competing ideas, simplify designs, give next-pixel instructions, and move builders into common Reddit or Discord venues; the shared practice is getting scattered help onto one plan.

second_order: keeping Solaire and its lettering intact
theme_note: Participants inspect damage, call defenders, touch up pixels, correct lettering, and report what still needs repair; the object under repair changes from figure to text, flame, or surrounding area.

second_order: joining the subreddit’s April Fools make-believe
theme_note: Posts and replies build, expose, preserve, or answer the room's own joke—from RIOT OR REMASTER to invented areas and fake help—rather than placing pixels on the canvas.

second_order: celebrating, admiring, and mourning what they made
theme_note: Participants recognize the emerging work, announce completion, admire it, or give it a post-close ending; the tone varies from triumph to regret and fading flame.

second_order: adding and redesigning Dark Souls pictures
theme_note: Participants propose or make additions around the inherited Solaire—yellow, a bonfire, a spirit bomb, a new figure, scenery, or an altered feature; proposals and completed additions remain distinguishable.

second_order: making room and deals with neighboring pictures
theme_note: Participants offer, accept, relay, or question arrangements over shared borders and pixels; the neighbours and degree of agreement vary, and proposals are not treated as completed deals.

second_order: meeting the Taskbar with resistance or a shared window
theme_note: Warnings, counter-calls, templates, border work, compromise, and integration plans all respond to the same approaching Taskbar; positions vary between fighting, moving, and adapting.

second_order: turning canvas work and damage into Dark Souls banter
theme_note: Participants recast pixels, voids, defacement, and approaching grey in the room's own playful language; the joke accompanies rather than replaces practical work.

second_order: answering why r/place is worth doing
theme_note: A skeptical question about caring for r/place receives the plain participant answer that it is fun.

second_order: disputing who gets to decide the shared plan
theme_note: Participants challenge decisions said to have been made in Discord and notice builders undoing one another when the design is unclear.

second_order: gathering place talk into approved threads and removing other proposals
theme_note: Moderators consolidate updates into a megathread or sticky and remove later proposals under the Dark Souls 1-only rule; consolidation and exclusion are different outcomes of venue control.

second_order: clearing up apparent sabotage with shared-plan knowledge
theme_note: Participants correct mistaken alarms by explaining intentional neighbouring pixels and using Discord knowledge to distinguish cooperation from sabotage.

second_order: sharing and reassuring over the same game mishap
theme_note: Two ordinary-game turns compare the same mishap and reassure another player; this selected-thread material belongs with no canvas practice.

second_order: trying to continue a Dark Souls spot after the canvas closed
theme_note: A surviving title proposes continuing on The Place 2.0; it is a post-event continuation attempt, not evidence that work resumed.
